title_en: Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Civil Trademark Dispute Cases

articles.content_en: Article 2 Where, in accordance with the provisions of Paragraph 1 of Article 13 of the Trademark Law, a person reproduces, imitates, or translates another person's well-known trademark that has not been registered in China or its main part and uses it as a trademark on the same or similar goods, which is likely to cause confusion, that person shall bear the civil liability for ceasing the infringement.

Article 4 The interested party as provided for in Article 53 of the Trademark Law shall include the licensee under a trademark license contract and the legal successor of the property right in the registered trademark, among others.
Where the exclusive right to use a registered trademark is infringed, the licensee under an exclusive license contract may institute legal proceedings with the People's Court; the licensee under a sole license contract may institute legal proceedings jointly with the trademark registrant, or may institute legal proceedings on its own if the trademark registrant does not institute legal proceedings; the licensee under an ordinary license contract may institute legal proceedings with the express authorization of the trademark registrant.

Article 5 Where a trademark registrant or an interested party files an application for renewal within the grace period for renewal of a registered trademark, before the application is approved, if the trademark registrant or interested party institutes legal proceedings on the ground that another person infringes its exclusive right to use the registered trademark, the People's Court shall accept the case.

Article 6 A civil action instituted for infringement of the exclusive right to use a registered trademark shall be under the jurisdiction of the People's Court of the place where the infringing act is committed, the place where the infringing goods are stored or sealed up or impounded, or the place of the domicile of the defendant, as provided for in Articles 13 and 52 of the Trademark Law.
The place where the infringing goods are stored as mentioned in the preceding paragraph shall mean the place where infringing goods are stored or concealed in large quantities or on a regular basis; the place where the infringing goods are sealed up or impounded shall mean the place where the infringing goods are sealed up or impounded by administrative authorities such as the customs and the industry and commerce administration according to law.

Article 7 For a joint action instituted against several defendants involving different places where the infringing acts are committed, the plaintiff may choose the People's Court of the place where one of the defendants commits the infringing act as the court of jurisdiction; for an action instituted only against one of the defendants, the People's Court of the place where that defendant commits the infringing act shall have jurisdiction.

Article 8 The relevant public as mentioned in the Trademark Law shall mean consumers related to a certain type of goods or services identified by the trademark and other business operators closely related to the marketing of the said goods or services.

Article 9 The identical trademark as provided for in Item (1) of Article 52 of the Trademark Law shall mean that the trademark alleged to infringe is compared with the plaintiff's registered trademark, and there is no visual difference between the two.
The similar trademark as provided for in Item (1) of Article 52 of the Trademark Law shall mean that when the trademark alleged to infringe is compared with the plaintiff's registered trademark, the font, pronunciation, meaning or the design and color of the figure, or the overall structure after the combination of its elements are similar, or the three-dimensional shape and color combination are similar, which is likely to cause the relevant public to misidentify the source of the goods or to consider that the source is specifically related to the goods of the plaintiff's registered trademark.

Article 11 Similar goods as provided for in Item (1) of Article 52 of the Trademark Law shall mean goods that are the same in terms of function, use, production department, sales channel, target consumers, or that the relevant public generally considers as having a specific connection and are likely to cause confusion.
Similar services shall mean services that are the same in terms of the purpose, content, method, and object of the service, or that the relevant public generally considers as having a specific connection and are likely to cause confusion.
Goods similar to services shall mean that there is a specific connection between the goods and the services, which is likely to cause confusion among the relevant public.

Article 12 When determining whether goods or services are similar in accordance with the provisions of Item (1) of Article 52 of the Trademark Law, the People's Court shall make a comprehensive judgment based on the general understanding of the goods or services by the relevant public; the International Classification of Goods and Services for the Purposes of the Registration of Marks and the Classification Table of Similar Goods and Services may serve as references for determining similar goods or services.

Article 13 When the People's Court determines the liability for damages of the infringer in accordance with the provisions of Paragraph 1 of Article 56 of the Trademark Law, the amount of damages may be calculated according to the calculation method chosen by the right holder.

Article 14 The profits gained from the infringement as provided for in Paragraph 1 of Article 56 of the Trademark Law may be calculated based on the product of the sales volume of the infringing goods and the unit profit of such goods; where the unit profit of such goods cannot be determined, it shall be calculated based on the unit profit of the goods bearing the registered trademark.

Article 15 The losses suffered from the infringement as provided for in Paragraph 1 of Article 56 of the Trademark Law may be calculated based on the reduction in the sales volume of the goods caused by the infringement to the right holder, or on the product of the sales volume of the infringing goods and the unit profit of the goods bearing the registered trademark.

Article 16 Where it is difficult to determine either the profits gained by the infringer from the infringement or the losses suffered by the infringed from the infringement, the People's Court may, upon request of a party or ex officio, apply the provisions of Paragraph 2 of Article 56 of the Trademark Law to determine the amount of damages.
When determining the amount of damages, the People's Court shall comprehensively consider factors such as the nature, duration, and consequences of the infringement, the reputation of the trademark, the amount of trademark license royalties, the type, time, and scope of the trademark license, and the reasonable expenses for curbing the infringement.
If the parties reach an agreement on the amount of damages in accordance with the provisions of Paragraph 1 of this Article, the agreement shall be permitted.

Article 17 The reasonable expenses paid for curbing the infringement as provided for in Paragraph 1 of Article 56 of the Trademark Law shall include the reasonable fees incurred by the right holder or authorized agent for investigating and obtaining evidence of the infringement.
The People's Court may, based on the claims of the parties and the specific circumstances of the case, include the attorney's fees that comply with the provisions of the relevant state authorities within the scope of damages.

Article 18 The limitation of action for infringement of the exclusive right to use a registered trademark shall be two years, calculated from the date when the trademark registrant or interested party knows or should have known the infringing act. Where the trademark registrant or interested party institutes legal proceedings after two years, if the infringing act continues at the time the proceedings are instituted and within the valid term of the exclusive right to use the registered trademark, the People's Court shall order the defendant to cease the infringing act, and the amount of damages for infringement shall be calculated retroactively for two years from the date when the right holder institutes legal proceedings with the People's Court.

Article 19 The failure to record a trademark license contract shall not affect the validity of the license contract, unless otherwise agreed by the parties.
If a trademark license contract is not recorded with the Trademark Office, it shall not be binding on a bona fide third party.

Article 20 The assignment of a registered trademark shall not affect the validity of a trademark license contract that has already taken effect before the assignment, unless otherwise provided in the trademark license contract.

Article 21 In hearing a case involving a dispute over infringement of the exclusive right to use a registered trademark, the People's Court may, in accordance with Article 134 of the General Principles of the Civil Law, Article 53 of the Trademark Law and the specific circumstances of the case, order the infringer to bear civil liabilities such as ceasing the infringement, removing obstacles, eliminating dangers, compensating for losses, and eliminating adverse effects, and may also make a civil sanction decision imposing a fine and confiscating the infringing goods, counterfeit trademark labels, and materials, tools, equipment and other property exclusively used for producing the infringing goods. The amount of the fine may be determined by reference to the relevant provisions of the Regulations on the Implementation of the Trademark Law of the People's Republic of China.
Where the administrative department for industry and commerce has already imposed an administrative penalty on the same act of infringement of the exclusive right to use a registered trademark, the People's Court shall not impose a civil sanction again.

Article 22 In hearing a trademark dispute case, the People's Court may, based on the request of a party and the specific circumstances of the case, determine whether the involved registered trademark is well-known according to law.
The determination of a well-known trademark shall be made in accordance with the provisions of Article 14 of the Trademark Law.
Where a party seeks protection for a trademark that has been previously determined as well-known by an administrative authority or the People's Court, if the other party does not raise an objection to the well-known status of the involved trademark, the People's Court shall not conduct a review. If an objection is raised, the People's Court shall conduct a review in accordance with Article 14 of the Trademark Law.
Article 23 The provisions of this Interpretation concerning goods trademarks shall apply to service trademarks.
Article 24 If any previous relevant provisions are inconsistent with this Interpretation, this Interpretation shall prevail.
